body.statement: For every fixed \(C_v<\infty\), compactness and linearity give \(\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}\lVert s(h,v)\rVert_\infty<\infty\). Because \(\delta_q>0\), all sufficiently large \(n\) satisfy \(\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}\lVert s(h,v)\rVert_\infty/\sqrt n<\delta_q\), so every positive or negative coordinate tilt obeys \(q_{n,ax\ell}(h,v)\ge q^0_{ax\ell}-|s(h,v)_{ax\ell}|/\sqrt n>\eta\). Uniformly on that domain, \(q_n(h,v)\in(\Delta_{L-1})^{2K}\), \(P_{p,q_n(h,v)}\in\mathcal M_\eta(p)\), and \(\sqrt n\,\theta_p(q_n(h,v))=h\). Moreover, for every bounded \(u\), some bounded nuisance coordinate \(v\) satisfies \(\sqrt n\{\tau(q_n(h,v))-\tau(q^0)\}=Qh+Nu\), while the remaining coordinates range over every common-arm-mean and zero-mean outcome-shape direction.
body.justification: This theorem verifies that the entire \(Qh+Nu\) treatment-effect fiber and every remaining shape nuisance form a legal local submodel for every finite support with \(L\ge2\); when \(L=2\), the zero-mean shape component correctly has dimension zero.
body.gap: Hirano and Porter localize regular models but do not construct the saturated finite-support fiber under design-dependent annotation.
body.consumer: The nuisance-uniform lower bound uses the full fiber, including every treatment-effect and outcome-shape tangent that leaves policy contrasts unchanged.
body.proof_tex:
Put \(c=(a,x)\).  Because \(L\ge 2\) and the values in \(\mathcal Y\) are distinct, each cell contains two indices \(u\ne w\) with \(y_u\ne y_w\).  The baseline belongs to \(\mathcal M_\eta(p)\), so \(q^0_{c\ell}\ge\eta>0\).  The variance identity
\[
 \sigma_c^2(q^0)=\sum_{\ell<m}q^0_{c\ell}q^0_{cm}(y_\ell-y_m)^2
\]
therefore gives \(\sigma_c^2(q^0)\ge\eta^2(y_u-y_w)^2>0\).  Define the cell tangent
\[
 m_{c\ell}=\frac{q^0_{c\ell}\{y_\ell-\mu_c(q^0)\}}
                         {\sigma_c^2(q^0)}.
\]
By the definitions of \(\mu_c(q^0)\) and \(\sigma_c^2(q^0)\),
\[
 \sum_{\ell=1}^L m_{c\ell}=0,
 \qquad
 \sum_{\ell=1}^L y_\ell m_{c\ell}=1.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus the cellwise restriction of \(B_{\mathrm{mean}}\) to the simplex tangent is onto \(\mathbb R\), including when \(L=2\).  Since \(\operatorname{rank}(F)=d\) by \(\mathrm{ass:menu\text{-}rank}\), \(A_{\mathrm{map}}=[-F\;F]\) has row rank \(d\).  Applying the cellwise right inverses in (1) shows that \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}=A_{\mathrm{map}}B_{\mathrm{mean}}\) is onto, consistently with the stipulated maps \(S_0\) and \(W\).

Fix \(C_v<\infty\).  The set
\(\mathcal H\times\{v:\lVert v\rVert\le C_v\}\) is compact, because \(\mathcal H\) is compact and the second factor is a closed bounded subset of a finite-dimensional space.  The map \((h,v)\mapsto S_0h+Wv\) is continuous.  Hence
\[
 C_s(C_v):=\sup_{h\in\mathcal H,\,\lVert v\rVert\le C_v}
             \lVert S_0h+Wv\rVert_\infty<\infty.
\tag{2}
\]
If \(n>\{C_s(C_v)/\delta_q\}^2\), then for every coordinate and every point of this compact parameter set,
\[
 q_{n,ax\ell}(h,v)
 =q^0_{ax\ell}+\frac{s(h,v)_{ax\ell}}{\sqrt n}
 \ge q^0_{ax\ell}-\frac{C_s(C_v)}{\sqrt n}
 >q^0_{ax\ell}-\delta_q\ge\eta.
\tag{3}
\]
Both \(S_0h\) and \(Wv\) lie in \(\mathcal E\), so each cell of \(s(h,v)\) sums to zero.  Consequently every cell of \(q_n(h,v)\) sums to one.  Equation (3), \(\mathrm{def:saturated\text{-}model}\), and its randomization and consistency member properties yield
\[
 q_n(h,v)\in(\Delta_{L-1})^{2K},
 \qquad P_{p,q_n(h,v)}\in\mathcal M_\eta(p),
\tag{4}
\]
uniformly on the stated domain.

The cell means are linear in \(q\).  Using \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}S_0=I_d\), \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}W=0\), and \(\mathrm{ass:tied\text{-}baseline}\), we obtain
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sqrt n\,\theta_p(q_n(h,v))
 &=\sqrt n\,\theta_p(q^0)+A_{\mathrm{map}}B_{\mathrm{mean}}s(h,v)\\
 &=A_{\mathrm{tan}}S_0h+A_{\mathrm{tan}}Wv=h.
 \end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]

It remains to establish exact nuisance coverage.  For each cell, every \(s_c\) in its simplex tangent has the unique decomposition
\[
 s_c=m_c b_c+k_c,
 \qquad b_c=\sum_{\ell=1}^L y_\ell s_{c\ell},
 \qquad
 \sum_{\ell=1}^L k_{c\ell}=sum_{\ell=1}^L y_\ell k_{c\ell}=0,
\tag{6}
\]
where (1) proves existence and uniqueness.  The cellwise shape space in (6) has dimension \(L-2\): the sum and mean functionals are linearly independent because the support contains two distinct values.  In particular, that dimension is zero when \(L=2\).

Let \(h\in\mathcal H\), let \(u\in\mathbb R^{K-d}\), let \(c\in\mathbb R^K\) be an arbitrary common-arm-mean direction, and choose arbitrary cellwise shape vectors \(k_{ax}\) satisfying the two equalities in (6).  Set
\[
 b_0=c,
 \qquad b_1=c+Qh+Nu,
 \qquad s^*_{ax}=m_{ax}b_{ax}+k_{ax}.
\tag{7}
\]
Equations (1) and (6) give \(B_{\mathrm{mean}}s^*=b\).  Since \(FQ=I_d\) and \(FN=0\),
\[
 A_{\mathrm{tan}}s^*=A_{\mathrm{map}}b
 =F(b_1-b_0)=F(Qh+Nu)=h.
\tag{8}
\]
Therefore \(s^*-S_0h\in\ker(A_{\mathrm{tan}})=\operatorname{im}(W)\).  The bijectivity of \(W\) supplies the unique coordinate
\[
 v=W^{-1}(s^*-S_0h).
\tag{9}
\]
All maps in (7)--(9) are linear between finite-dimensional spaces, so bounded sets of \((h,u,c,k)\) map to bounded sets of \(v\).  In particular, taking \(c=0\) and \(k=0\) proves the claimed realization of every bounded treatment-effect direction \(Qh+Nu\); varying \(c\) and \(k\) independently gives every common-arm-mean and zero-mean outcome-shape direction.

Finally, these nuisance coordinates exhaust rather than merely embed in the kernel.  Their dimensions are
\[
 K+(K-d)+2K(L-2)=2K(L-1)-d=\dim\ker(A_{\mathrm{tan}}),
\tag{10}
\]
where the last equality uses surjectivity of \(A_{\mathrm{tan}}\).  The decomposition (6) and the direct decomposition \(b_0=c\), \(b_1=c+Nu\) of \(\ker(A_{\mathrm{map}})\) show that the sum in (10) is direct.  This proves full coverage also at the binary-support endpoint \(L=2\).
